datasets.name: approved_decisions
queryLines:
SELECT decision_id, approved_at, CAST(approved_at AS DATE) AS approval_date,
       movie_id, movie_title, action,
       CASE WHEN theater_id = '' THEN 'All theaters' ELSE theater_id END AS theater_scope,
       period_start, period_end, approver_email, approval_note,
       source_table, evidence_json
FROM decision_feedback
ORDER BY approved_at DESC, decision_id DESC

measures.name: total_movies
measures.expr: COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN TRIM(movie_id) <> '' AND LOWER(TRIM(movie_id)) <> 'unknown' THEN movie_id END)

config.comment: Theater daily sales metrics for March 2026. Row-level security is enforced by the underlying table's row filter (theater managers see their theater, zone managers see their zone, leadership sees all).

lines:
## Approved leadership decisions

Source: `theater_analytics.gold.decision_feedback`. Approval dates refer to when leadership approved; sales-period dates refer to the reviewed evidence. This page is independent of the sales-page filters. Approval records decisions only, not schedule changes. Empty results mean no recorded approvals match the filters. Run the feedback setup notebook and grant the dashboard query identity SELECT before using this page. Access to this audit table is separate from sales-table row filters.

### Key insights
* **IMAX premium is the biggest lever** — IMAX tickets average $16.81 vs $12.29 for Standard (+37%), yet IMAX is only ~7% of showings.
* **Ratings don't sell tickets** — IMDb rating vs revenue correlation is ~0.05; avg revenue per screen-day is flat across rating buckets. Program on genre mix, not ratings.
* **No weekend effect** — avg revenue per screen-day is ~$35–36 every day of the week.
* **Geography is concentrated** — CA and TX drive ~27% of total revenue.
* **Data quality** — ~1% of rows have a null show date, ~2.7K rows lack seat capacity, and 185 theaters have an 'Unknown' zone manager.
* **Privacy note** — row-level security applies: each viewer sees only their authorized theaters.

frame.title: Distinct Movies Played
frame.description: Distinct known movie IDs in Gold sales for the selected filters and dates; not a live schedule.

lines:
### How to use this page

* **Movie filter**: select one or more titles to filter the count, performance views, and theater/state listings together.
* **Distinct Movies Played**: counts distinct known movie IDs in Gold sales within the selected dates and filters, not current schedules. Repeated sales across days, formats, screens, or theaters do not increase the count.
* **Movie theaters and states**: one row per movie ID, theater, and state with sales in the selected scope. The theater label includes its ID to distinguish repeated names.
* **Existing performance metrics**: Revenue per Showing uses daily Gold row counts, not scheduled screenings; Occupancy Rate lacks a screening-level capacity denominator. Do not treat either as proof to change schedules.
* All views respect the Gold row filter and the dashboard's execution identity.

frame.title: Movie Theaters and States
frame.description: Locations with Gold sales in the selected dates and filters; not a current screening schedule.

frame.title: Top 10 Movies by Revenue per Showing

lines:
### How to use this page

* **Pricing vs occupancy matrix** (top left): each bubble is a theater. High occupancy + low avg ticket price → pricing power; test premium pricing or premium (IMAX) formats. Low occupancy + high price → consider promotions or reprogramming.
* **Top 10 by seats sold / occupancy**: volume and fill-rate leaders — compare their format and screen mix.
* **Revenue by state x screen type**: where premium screens pay off by region — useful for IMAX conversion planning.
* **Detail table**: click any column header to sort. All views respect row-level security — you only see data for your authorized theaters.
